question:
Summarize the following in four sentences or less.:
The new Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles movie has a common MCU problem
Michael Boyle
Wed, August 2, 2023 at 6:35 a.m. GMT-4·5 min read
teenage mutant ninja turtles mutant mayhem
TMNT: Mutant Mayhem has a common MCU problemParamount
One of the most powerful moments in superhero movie history is that "What's Up Danger" montage in Spider-Man: Into the Spider-Verse.

It's a moment where the main character Miles takes a leap of faith off a building and, as a result, finally grows into the superhero role he's been afraid of this whole time. Although Spider-Verse is definitely a fun, kid-friendly movie with no shortage of jokes throughout, these two minutes are played completely straight.

When the "camera" flips upside down to portray a rising Miles as he's falling through the air, it's an unironically epic moment, and the movie's comfortable with staying in this tone until the montage is completely over.

There is no such sequence in Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles: Mutant Mayhem.

teenage mutant ninja turtles mutant mayhem
Paramount
Related: Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles bosses confirm movie sequel

The closest thing we get is the scene where April O'Neil, terrified of puking again on live TV, decides to go on camera to defend her turtle friends.

For a moment it looks like her nerves are about to get the best of her once again, but she manages to pull herself together and protect her friends in their moment of need. (And as a bonus, she gets the journalistic scoop of a lifetime.)

But then the triumphant music cuts short and she vomits all over the place in the middle of her speech. Sure, her character growth continues unabated afterward, but the movie just couldn't help throwing in that vomit gag right in the middle. God forbid a character here is allowed to have a proper, uninterrupted moment where they get to be cool.

Mutant Mayhem is filled with moments like these. Every time a scene threatens to get a little too serious, a little too real, there's some gag thrown in to undermine that tone.

teenage mutant ninja turtles mutant mayhem
Paramount
When the turtles are devastated by the belief that they'll never be accepted by humans, there are jokes. When Splinter's realising his flaws as a father for the first time, there are jokes. Even when the turtles are in the middle of being crushed to death by the villain, the movie's still throwing in a dozen quips a minute.

At no point does it feel like anyone's in danger; at no point does it feel like any character could fail in a way that matters.

This is a storytelling tendency that's frustratingly familiar to a lot of MCU fans: whether it's Korg in Thor: Ragnarok making quips right after Asgard's been destroyed, or Mantis from Guardians of the Galaxy Vol 2 getting hit in the head by debris in the middle of a heroic circle shot, it's clear that Marvel often can't resist undermining its cool or serious moments.

There's a lot of risk in being sincere – it means some viewers might think you're being sappy, or cringe – and a lot of MCU movies seem terrified of taking that risk. Although Mutant Mayhem is still a fun, exciting movie that'll should be a big hit, it's a shame it decided to follow the MCU's footsteps in this specific regard.

yondu michael rooker, nebula karen gillan, star lordpeter quill chris pratt, gamora zoe saldana, mantis pom klementieff, drax dave bautista, rocket voiced by bradley cooper and groot voiced by vin diesel
Disney
Of course, it's not the MCU that most audiences will compare Mutant Mayhem to. Instead, the likely comparison is Into the Spider-Verse, and Mayhem should have followed that movie more than the MCU.

Both are animated PG action movies filled with comedy, but Spider-Verse has the invaluable ability to know when to take itself seriously. We know this not just because of what's in the film itself, but what the Spider-Verse creators chose to leave on the cutting room floor.

That "What's Up Danger" scene wasn't always the triumphant, tonally-consistent sequence we got in the final product; originally, Miles was supposed to slam through a truck while swinging. The music would have jarringly cut short, and we'd watch as Miles landed against a brick wall with a humorous thud and a dopey groan of pain.

"It never felt quite right," the movie's feature animation editor Andy Leviton explained on Twitter back in 2019.

"After watching the whole movie in that state it truly felt like it was missing something. This was only a few months before release, [so] we scrambled in edit to mock up a more triumphant ending."

Fun #SpiderVerse Fact!
3010 MRU - Miles Rise Up. The number is for organization in editorial and the acronym/name goes across all departments. It was one of the few sequences that was in the movie from the very beginning back in early 2016 and was re-boarded/recut until... https://t.co/zBt3m5RZ1H

— Andy! Leviton (@AlliterAndy) January 29, 2019

In other words, Miles' clumsy fall was the Spider-Verse version of April O'Neil vomiting in the middle of her triumphant news broadcast.

You could see the appeal of this version of Miles' fall from a studio perspective: it was funny (sort of), and it would pre-emptively address any potential accusations that this movie might think too highly of itself. Ultimately though, the creators correctly chose at the last minute to change it to something better.

It's a shame Mutant Mayhem never seemed to make any similar choices.

teenage mutant ninja turtles mutant mayhem
Paramount
Maybe the best, most effective emotional moment in Mutant Mayhem is the early scene where the turtles are heading back into the sewer after a night out in the human world.

One of them stays there with the sewer pothole slightly open, taking a last lingering look at the city he knows he'll never truly be a part of. For just a few seconds the movie simply lets its audience sit with the character's sadness.

Mutant Mayhem is definitely a fun movie, but if it'd been comfortable holding onto emotional notes like it did in that one early scene, it could have been a truly great one too.

In reality, it wasn’t until the twentieth century that authors began to make “representational attempts to capture the intrinsic qualities of a child, its point of view, its voice, its language, and its rhythms.” (Approaching childhood in contemporary Britain Sandra Dinter). The shift in perception towards children is largely accredited to the literary figures of the Romantic epoch, who venerated children and viewed them as a vehicle for expressing their discontent with the existing society. Victor Hugo’s bold claim that “Christopher Columbus only discovered America, I discovered the child!” (A history of childhood: children and childhood in the west from…Colin Heywood. Cite 32) reflects the paradigm shift in which childhood was idealized as a sacred state blessed by the Divine and an eternal source of inspiration. (A history of childhood: children and childhood in the west from…Colin Heywood). The Romantic writers were fascinated with the concept of the ‘noble savage,’ a figure uncorrupted by societal constraints and possessing an innate, untainted morality. This idea, popularized by Jean-Jacques Rousseau, saw childhood as a time of unspoiled innocence and imagination and posited that the child’s unblemished nature provided a window into the essence of humanity. Consequently, the Romantics’ infatuation with childlike language and perspective inspired them to integrate child narrators and their purity into their literary oeuvre. For instance, Wordsworth and Blake, among others, “used childhood as a critical criterion from which the fallen state of modern society could be measured and condemned- and as a divine resource through which it could possibly be redeemed.” (Critical children: the use of childhood in ten great novels. P 9) Moreover, the child narrator’s presence in Romantic literature served as a critique of the prevailing rationalism and empiricism that dominated the Enlightenment era. By privileging the child’s intuitive and imaginative capacities, Romantic authors sought to challenge the notion that reason and logic were the sole arbiters of truth. In doing so, they emphasized the importance of the individual’s subjective experience and the transformative power of the imagination.

(In the school literature clubroom…)

Monika: “There! Everything’s all set for today’s club meeting.”

Sayori: “Thanks, Monika! I can’t wait to see everyone and share some poems.”

Natsuki: “I hope we have some snacks this time. I’m starving.”

Yuri: “I brought some tea for us to enjoy during our discussion. I find it really helps to set the mood for reading and sharing.”

Monika: “I’m glad you all came prepared. It’s important to create a welcoming and inspiring atmosphere for our members. I honestly feel like a beached whale with this baby bump, but I can’t wait to see everyone’s creativity shine through their poems.”

Sayori: “Don’t worry, Monika! You’re still the best club president ever! Plus, your baby bump just makes you even more adorable.”

Natsuki: “Yeah, you’re like our cute little mama bear. And with all these snacks and tea, I’m sure today’s meeting will be a blast.”

Yuri: “I agree. Let’s make today’s meeting a memorable one, filled with laughter and inspiration.”

Monika: “Thank you, everyone. I’m so grateful to have such supportive and talented friends in this club. Let’s make today’s meeting one to remember!”

(Soon, more members start arriving, each carrying their own poems and eager to share their thoughts.)

Monika: “Welcome, everyone! I’m so glad to see you all here. Let’s begin with our discussion of last week’s readings and then move on to sharing our own poems. Remember, this club is a safe space for us to express ourselves and grow as writers.”

Sayori: “I’ll go first! I wrote a poem about the beauty of nature and how it brings me a sense of peace. I hope you all enjoy it.”

Natsuki: “I wrote a poem about friendship and how it can lift us up in times of darkness. I tried to add a touch of humor to it, so I hope you like it.”

Yuri: “I wrote a poem about the endless depths of the ocean and the mysteries it holds. I find it fascinating how something so vast and unknown can be so captivating.”

Monika: “Thank you, everyone, for sharing your work. Each poem was truly special and unique. Now, let’s take some time to discuss and provide feedback to each other. Remember, constructive criticism is key to helping us improve as writers.”

(The club meeting continues in a positive and supportive atmosphere, with members encouraging each other and sharing their love for literature and poetry.)

Monika: “I’m so proud of the incredible talent and creativity in this club. Thank you all for being here today and for sharing your wonderful poems. Let’s continue to inspire each other and make this club a place where we can all grow and learn toge- OWWWW!!! Oh, God, it hurts!”

(The club members look over at Monika, who is clutching her stomach in pain.)

Sayori: “Monika, are you okay? What’s wrong?”

Monika: “I think…I think I’m having contractions! This shouldn’t have happened…I’m not due for another two months!”

Natsuki: “Oh no, we need to get you to the hospital!”

Yuri: “Quick, someone call an ambulance!”

(The club members quickly spring into action, calling for help and assisting Monika as best as they can.)

Monika: “I’m sorry, everyone…I didn’t expect this to happen during our club meeting…”

Sayori: “Don’t worry about that now, Monika. Your health and the baby’s well-being are the most important things. Just focus on staying calm.”

Monika: “I just hope labor doesn’t happen so fast…”

Natsuki: “Just breathe, Monika. We’re here for you, no matter what. We’ll make sure you and the baby are taken care of.”

Yuri: “Everything will be okay, Monika. Just hold on and stay strong. We’ll get through this together.”

(As they wait for the ambulance to arrive, the club members stick by Monika’s side, offering words of comfort and support.)

Monika: “Thank you, everyone…for being here for me. I don’t know what I would do without all of you.”

Sayori: “We’re a family, Monika. We take care of each other, no matter what. And we’ll be here every step of the way.”

(Moments later, however, it becomes clear that the ambulance won’t arrive in time. Monika’s contractions are getting stronger, and with a loud scream of pain, she suddenly goes into labor right there in the clubroom.)

Sayori: “Oh my goodness! Monika, hang in there! We’ll help you through this!”

Natsuki: “Just breathe, Monika. You’ve got this!”

Yuri: “Stay strong, Monika. We’re here to support you.”

(The club members work together to assist Monika in giving birth, doing their best to keep her comfortable and calm.)

Monika: (panting) “I-I can’t do this! It hurts too much!”

Sayori: “You can do this, Monika! Just keep breathing and pushing. We’re all here for you.”

Natsuki: “You’re doing great, Monika! Just a little bit more, you’ve got this!”

Yuri: “Stay focused, Monika. You’re almost there. Keep pushing with all your strength.”

(With one final push, Monika gives birth to a healthy baby, who lets out a small cry as it enters the world.)

Monika: (crying) “Oh my goodness…my baby…Miyuki…”

Sayori: “Congratulations, Monika! You did it! Miyuki is beautiful!”

Natsuki: “She’s perfect, just like her mama. I’m so happy for you, Monika.”

Yuri: “Welcome to the world, Miyuki. You are loved and cherished by all of us here.”

Monika: “Thank you, everyone. I couldn’t have done it without your support. I’m so grateful to have you all as my friends.”

(The club members gather around Monika and Miyuki, embracing them in a warm and loving hug.)

Monika: “I may have given birth during a club meeting, but I wouldn’t have it any other way. This moment will always hold a special place in my heart.”

Sayori: “This just proves the bond we all share as friends and club members. We truly are family.”

Natsuki: “Yeah, who knew a literature club meeting could turn into a birthing event? But hey, that’s just how we roll!”

Yuri: “No matter what life throws at us, we will always be here to support and uplift each other. That’s what friendship is all about.”

(And as the club members celebrate the birth of little Miyuki, they know that their bond and friendship will only continue to grow stronger with each passing day.)

{EIGHT YEARS LATER}

(At Monika’s place…)

Monika: “And that, my little girl, is how you first entered my life while I was still in school.”

Miyuki: “Wow, Mom! That’s such a cool story! I can’t believe I was born during a literature club meeting.”

Monika: “It was definitely a memorable moment, that’s for sure. But the most important thing is that you came into this world healthy and loved.”

Miyuki: “I’m so grateful to have such an amazing mom and such wonderful friends who were there for you during that time.”

Monika: “And I’m grateful for you, my sweet Miyuki. You bring so much joy and love into my life every day.”

Miyuki: “I love you, Mom.”

Monika: “I love you too, Miyuki. Get some sleep, okay? You have a big day of school tomorrow.”

Miyuki: “Okay, Mom. Goodnight!”

Monika: “Goodnight, sweetheart.”

(As Monika watches her daughter head off to bed, she can’t help but feel grateful for the incredible bond she shares with her friends from the literature club. They may have started as a group of students with a shared love for poetry, but they had become a true family, supporting each other through the highs and lows of life. And as she reflects on the journey that led her to this moment, Monika knows that she is truly blessed to have such wonderful people in her life.)

"The theme of 0-1 and 0-3, "Into The Fire", sets the standard for most songs in the game to follow; starting with a slow and ominous buildup in the intro portion of the song, before promptly welcoming in the meat and potatoes of the track with a mechanical screech that lies somewhere between Brown Note and satisfying ecstasy, before turning into pure, hectic, drum n' bass bliss, with many more Amen Breaks to follow.
"Unstoppable Force", the theme of 0-2 and 0-4, starts off deceptively slow with a laid-back, funky bassline. Not even mere seconds later, the intensity kicks itself back into top gear as the backing guitar from "Into The Fire" comes back with a vengeance.
"Cerberus", the theme of 0-5 and the first major boss theme in the game, acts as a firm welcome to your final obstacle(s) between you and the gates of Hell, being a slow, yet no doubt intense track that, combined with the fact that this was the first track composed for the game, sure leaves a lasting impression.
After the industrial hellhouse that was Prelude, you take your first steps into Hell in its entirety, and what ends up greeting you is "A Thousand Greetings", the first song you'll hear upon stepping into Limbo for the very first time and the textbook definition of Dissonant Serenity. Despite how calming it sounds, the additional reverb that plays over it help give the idea that something is off.
Not long after your first few minutes in Limbo, the carnage finally starts with the battle theme of 1-1, "A Shattered Illusion", finally revealing to you that this seemingly wonderful, beautiful place is nothing more than a visage made to drive sinners insane.
Building on from that is the battle theme of 1-2, the aptly named "A Complete and Utter Destruction of The Senses". A deranged breakcore track full of off-beat notes and mechanical screeches that perfectly encapsulates the blazing hell brought on by the Streetcleaners before you.
The theme of 1-3, "Castle Vein", as the name implies, is a DnB love letter to the music of the Castlevania series.
After three levels of pure chaos in a land that doesn't really exist, 1-4 greets you with a beautiful rendition of Claude Debussy's "Clair de Lune"; the serenity of the piece, combined with the artificial night sky and empty mansion, provides a moment of respite after everything you have been through up until this point. However, it doesn't last long...
"Versus", V2's theme, combines pulse-pounding drumbeats with rocking guitars and a smooth bass intro, perfect for a clash between two opponents of equal strength.
"Cold Winds" acts as the desolate and ominous introduction to the doomed layer of Lust in stage 2-1, and what an introduction it is.
2-2 introduces you to "Requiem", which takes the ominous beat of "Cold Winds" and adds a beautiful MIDI violin on top of it, encapsulating the tragedy of the ghost town you're blitzing through to a T.
The theme of 2-3, "Panic Betrayer" kicks the intensity and beats back up to eleven as Lust starts throwing out some of the deadlier waves of enemies you have faced up until this point.
At the end of Lust, you are greeted with the theme of 2-4, as well as the battle theme of The Corpse of King Minos, "In The Presence of A King", a truly bleak track that provides plenty of eerie buildup as you walk through the tunnels of Lust before exploding into a truly horrifying Drone of Dread as you trade blows with the colossal Husk that stands before you.
Finally, at the end of Act I, lies your final hurdle before the beginning of the end: The Gluttony layer, which is introduced with "Guts", a harrowing, slasher movie-esque synth piece that lays bare the absolute Body Horror before you. Midway through however, the synth picks up a pitch and the sheer terror brought upon by "Guts" swiftly turns into sheer determination as the heavy amen break beat and uneasy piano courtesy of "Glory" kicks in.
As you take your first steps into 3-2, you are greeted by a foreboding Gregorian choir that seems to get louder and louder as you progress your way through the level. Eventually, a voice starts speaking out to you, as the choir fades out and into an absolutely glorious electric organ cover of Bach's "I call to you, Lord Jesus Christ". It is only there and then do you realize who exactly you'll be dealing with.
Gabriel's first battle theme: "Divine Intervention". Whilst short, looping at only 48 seconds, is an undeniably epic piece fitting for one of the most powerful, deadly, and self-righteous foes you will face in your quest for blood.
"Disgrace. Humiliation.", the ending theme of Act I, is a short music box track that laments Gabriel's pathetic state at the feet of the Council as a new hatred starts to burn within him.
The theme of the Secret Level 1-S, "Sanctuary in The Garden of The Mind", is absolutely beautiful and fits perfectly for a Breather Level such as this.
The theme of 2-S, "Sunshine", defies explanation. All that can really be said is that it starts off relatively cheery and upbeat before things take a strange turn.
P-1 takes the cake with three songs that could arguably be considered some of Hakita's best musical work.
First off, we have "The Spinal Staircase", which serves as the intro music to the stage. What starts off as an uneasy recording of Maurice Depret's "Sourire d'Avril"note  soon devolves into absolute horror as the song slowly turns into horrible, distorted static the further you descend down the titular staircase.
The theme of the Flesh Prison, "CHAOS", couldn't have a more fitting name. Having absolutely no sense of time signatures and consisting of nothing but wailing guitars and maniacal beats, a fight this chaotic deserves an equally chaotic track.
Finally, we have "ORDER", the theme of Minos Prime. What starts off with a beautiful violin solo turns into an intense DnB metal hybrid, topped of with a Dark Reprise of "Requiem", tying together an absolutely legendary piece that brings the heroism and tragedy of King Minos full circle. Couldn't be any more fitting for one of the hardest bosses in the game."

tell me how the text below responds to the question-How are rhetorical and figurative devices used to engage the listener?: The Pleasure of Books
The habit of reading is one of the greatest resources of mankind; and we enjoy reading
books that belong to us much more than if they are borrowed. A borrowed book is like a guest
in the house; it must be treated with punctiliousness, with a certain considerate formality.
You must see that it sustains no damage; it must not suffer while under your roof. You cannot
5 leave it carelessly, you cannot mark it, you cannot turn down the pages, you cannot use
it familiarly. And then, some day, although this is seldom done, you really ought to return it.
But your own books belong to you; you treat them with that affectionate intimacy that
annihilates formality. Books are for use, not for show; you should own no book that you are
afraid to mark up, or afraid to place on the table, wide open and face down. A good reason
10 for marking favorite passages in books is that this practice enables you to remember more
easily the significant sayings, to refer to them quickly, and then in later years, it is like visiting a
forest where you once blazed a trail. You have the pleasure of going over the old ground, and
recalling both the intellectual scenery and your own earlier self.
Everyone should begin collecting a private library in youth; the instinct of private property,
15 which is fundamental in human beings, can here be cultivated with every advantage and no
evils. One should have one’s own bookshelves, which should not have doors, glass windows,
or keys; they should be free and accessible to the hand as well as to the eye. The best of
mural decorations is books; they are more varied in color and appearance than any wallpaper,
they are more attractive in design, and they have the prime advantage of being separate
20 personalities, so that if you sit alone in the room in the firelight, you are surrounded with intimate
friends. The knowledge that they are there in plain view is both stimulating and refreshing. You
do not have to read them all. Most of my indoor life is spent in a room containing six thousand
books; and I have a stock answer to the invariable question that comes from strangers. “Have
you read all of these books?” “Some of them twice.” This reply is both true and unexpected.
25 There are of course no friends like living, breathing, corporeal men and women; my
devotion to reading has never made me a recluse. How could it? Books are of the people,
by the people, for the people. Literature is the immortal part of history; it is the best and most
enduring part of personality. But book-friends have this advantage over living friends; you can
enjoy the most truly aristocratic society in the world whenever you want it. The great dead are
30 beyond our physical reach, and the great living are usually almost as inaccessible; as for our
personal friends and acquaintances, we cannot always see them. Perchance1 they are asleep,
or away on a journey. But in a private library, you can at any moment converse with Socrates
or Shakespeare or Carlyle or Dumas or Dickens or Shaw or Barrie or Galsworthy. And there is
no doubt that in these books you see these men at their best. They wrote for you. They “laid
35 themselves out,” they did their ultimate best to entertain you, to make a favorable impression.
You are necessary to them as an audience is to an actor; only instead of seeing them masked2,
you look into their innermost heart of heart.
Radio address by William Lyon Phelps3 (6 April, 1933) USA

There is a low threat of new entrants, this is due to the high set up costs associated creating a new airline, some of the costs include: airport fees, purchases of planes, training requirements. Despite the high barriers to entry of the airline industry, if a new competitor were to enter then consumers may initially be hesitant due to a lack of brand reputation. 
However, if an existing competitor were to change their business model to low-cost flights then this would pose a threat to Ryanair. 

Threat of substitutes 
For the airline industry there isn’t currently a direct substitute. The closest alternative to air travel is trains. However, the compete with all modes of transport. With the introduction of high-speed rails, this can reduce the travel times of trains and the advantage of not being restricted in luggage weight, therefore consumers may choose to use the high-speed trains over air travel. However, trains are unable to take passengers to all the destinations as planes are able to. This is because of the sea, therefore there would need to be development of more tunnels like the euro-tunnel. 

Bargaining power of suppliers 
As there are few aeroplane manufacturers, Boeing and Airbus being 2 of the main competitors for aeroplane manufacturing. This results in high switching costs between manufacturers. Currently Ryanair’s fleet is supplied by Boeing, with a recent deal for 300 new Boeing aircrafts. Suppliers of fuel can affect the profitability of Ryanair as if fuel prices increase then the Ryanair has to decide whether they incur the cost or pass it along to customers. But as their customers are typically price sensitive this could result in a higher operating costs as flights continue to run with fewer passengers 

Bargaining power of buyers 
Consumers have a relatively high level of bargaining power. Airlines compete for brand loyalty of consumers. This is because there a variety of airline providers that offer similar services to Ryanair. Buyers can also use word of mouth to share their experiences with the airline to create bad press, which can tarnish reputations. Ryanair is familiar with bad press such as the family who paid £165 to check in after an online check in error. 

Rivalry among existing competitors 
There is high levels of competition within the airline industry as a result of levels of regulation regarding health and safety. Ryanair competes within the low-cost carriers, some of the main competitors include EasyJet, Wizz Air, KLM. The airlines compete for customer loyalty and market share. EasyJet currently has a larger market share than Ryanair. Within the low-cost carriers they compete to provide high quality services at the lowest price to consumers possible while generating a profit. When advertising Ryanair focus on the cost of the flights they offer while EasyJet focus on creating memories.

question:
(In the clubroom…)

Monika: “Wait a minute…where’s Natsuki?”

Sayori: “I honestly don’t know.”

Yuri: “No idea.”

Monika: “Yuri, Sayori, can you go look for her? I’ll just…stay here.”

Sayori: “Of course, Monika! We’ll find her.”

Yuri: “Yes, we’ll search the school grounds and see if she’s anywhere nearby. Let’s go, Sayori.”

(Sayori and Yuri leave the clubroom and start searching for Natsuki. Once the two girls are gone, Monika rubs her belly lovingly - eagerly awaiting the arrival of her unborn daughter; Minika.)

Monika: (whispering to herself) “Soon, Minika…soon, I’ll be able to hold you in my arms. I can’t wait to meet you, my little girl.”

(As if responding to Monika’s voice, her belly ripples slightly.)

Monika: “Aww, you’re so active today, aren’t you, Minika? You must be excited too, huh? Just a little while longer, and we’ll finally be together. I’ll be the best mommy I can be for you, I promise. I can’t wait for you to meet my friends.”

(Inside the school…)

Sayori: “Do you think Natsuki might be in the cafeteria? She did mention being hungry earlier.”

Yuri: “It’s worth checking. Let’s head over there first.”

(They walk towards the cafeteria, scanning the room for any sign of Natsuki. Finally, they spot her sitting alone at a table, her head resting on her arms.)

Sayori: “Natsuki! There you are!”

(Natsuki looks up, wiping away a few stray tears from her eyes.)

Natsuki: “Oh, hey guys. What are you doing here?”

Yuri: “Monika sent us to look for you. We were worried when you didn’t show up at the club.”

Sayori: “Is everything okay, Natsuki?”

(Natsuki hesitates for a moment, then sighs.)

Natsuki: “I’ve been having a rough day… Is it alright if I talk to you guys about it?”

(Sayori and Yuri exchange concerned glances before nodding.)

Yuri: “Of course, Natsuki. We’re here for you.”

(Back in the clubroom…)

Monika: (smiling at her belly) “I hope the girls find Natsuki soon. They can be such good friends for you, Minika. They’ll be there for you, just like they’ve always been for me.”

(Monika strokes her belly gently, filled with anticipation and love.)

Monika: “We’re going to have such a wonderful journey together, my sweet Minika. I can’t wait to see what the future holds for us.”

(Just then, an extreme wave of pain courses through Monika’s body.)

Monika: “Aah! Wh-what’s happening? This…this isn’t normal…”

(In a panic, Monika grabs her phone and dials 911. She frantically explains her symptoms and requests an ambulance. Moments later, an ambulance arrives at the school and rushes Monika to the hospital.)

Monika: (strained voice) “Please…please, be okay, Minika. Mama will do everything she can to keep you safe…”

(At the hospital, Monika is rushed into the maternity ward.)

Monika: “Doctor, what’s wrong with me?! Why am I feeling this pain?!”

Doctor: “Monika, please try to stay calm. We’re doing everything we can to figure out what’s going on. We’ll run some tests and monitor your condition closely.”

(Monika’s heart races as the doctors and nurses rush around her, hooking her up to various machines and administering medication.)

Monika: (teary-eyed) “Please, just tell me if my baby is going to be alright. I can’t lose her.”

Doctor: “I understand how important this is to you, Monika. We’ll do our best to ensure the safety of both you and your baby. Just try to stay as relaxed as you can for now.”

(Several agonizing hours pass as Monika waits anxiously for news. Finally, a doctor comes out to speak with her.)

Doctor: “Monika, I have good news. Your baby is stable, but we did discover some complications. It seems that you’ve been experiencing contractions, which is premature labor.”

Monika: “Premature labor? But it’s too early… What does this mean for my baby?”

Doctor: “We’re doing everything we can to delay the labor and give your baby more time to develop. We’ve administered medication and will continue to closely monitor both of you. However, I must be honest with you, Monika. There are risks involved with premature birth, and we’ll need to prepare for all possible outcomes.”

(Monika’s heart sinks as she absorbs the doctor’s words. She holds her belly tightly, praying for the well-being of her daughter.)

Monika: “Please, do whatever you can to keep her safe. I’ll do anything, just please…”

Doctor: “We’re doing everything we can, Monika. We’ll keep you updated on any changes or developments. In the meantime, try to rest and stay as calm as possible. We’re here for you.”

(Monika nods, tears streaming down her face, as she grips onto the hope that her baby will survive this ordeal. She closes her eyes, sending all her love and strength to her unborn daughter, Minika. Suddenly, Monika’s water breaks - signaling that the labor had progressed much faster than normal.)

question:
summarize this without paraphrasing it in 300 words"
The purpose of this research study was to examine the effect of sports sponsorship on the promotion of sports events. While scholars have explored the main reasons why corporations sponsor sports events, they have not illustrated the overall effects of sponsorship on the promotion of the  events and the factors affecting these outcomes. For this study, a quantitative approach with the use of a questionnaire was adopted; data were collected  from 400 managers and organisers of sports events. The research questions addressed how the brand image of the sponsors improves when they sponsor sports events and what effect sponsorship has on the success of the events. Our findings showed that businesses that sponsor sports event gain improved brand image, increased exposure to customers and increased sales. Sports event managers and individual players also benefit from sponsorships. The study findings indicated that sponsors give technical, expert and financial support in exchange for improved brand awareness and brand image, which ultimately increases their revenues. The importance and popularity of sports over the past 50 years have given rise to a new industry, the sports industry. The past three decades have seen significant growth in this industry (Saeed et al., 2014). The fantasy sports industry relies highly on efficient customer relationship management (CRM) for much of its success. The ability for a provider to deliver quick, accurate and descriptive information to its consumers will result in customer loyalty and retention (Smith et al., 2010). Major sports events have become an important feature of global business and sports sponsorship has increased because professional sports organisations cannot function effectively without the revenues generated from commercial activities (Faed et al., 2012). Sports organisations rely on the sale of telecasting/broadcasting  rights, sponsorship income and ticket sales to hold sports events. The present study focused on the revenue stream generated from sponsorship because it is a major source of funding for many sports organisations. In 2017, expenditures on sports sponsorship were approximately USD 16.62 billion in North America; this number is expected to reach USD 19.88 billion by 2021. Total worldwide sponsorship spending in 2012 was USD 40 billion and is predicted to reach USD 62.7 billion by 2018 (Statista, 2018). Sports sponsorship plays a significant role in promoting and financing various games (Houghton et al., 2014). Donlan (2014) explained that, although sports sponsorship significantly helps to build consumer-based brand equity, a range of factors, including the strength of the sponsor-event and the leverage of activities affects it. According to him, the most successful sponsorships contribute to brand quality and brand loyalty. Koronios et al. (2016) claimed that sports sponsorships promote various sports through the provision of funds as well as sponsors’ products and services. A special strategy known as ‘event marketing’, which has developed over the past three decades, has been adapted to promote companies’ products and services when an event is sponsored. According to BusinessDictionary.com (2018), “event marketing is the activity of designing or developing a themed activity, occasion, display, or exhibit (such as a sporting event, music festival, fair, or concert) to promote a product, cause, or organization.” A sub-theme of event marketing is ‘marketing through sports’, in  which major sports events like the Olympic Games, the Union of European Football Associations (UEFA) Champions League, the World Marathon Majors and the Fédération Internationale de Football Association (FIFA) World Cup are sponsored and live advertisements of companies’ products and services are shown continuously. This is a big boost for marketing (Lynn and Close, 2011). The funding of sports events can be extended to various levels, from small-town or city-level events to world-level competitions such as the Olympics Games. As an example of the latter, Toyota signed an eight-year, USD 1.64 billion deal with the International Olympic Committee in 2015, covering the years 2017 to 2024 (Sport Business, 2016). The other four firms involved in the top five sports sponsorship deals  of 2015 were AB InBev [USD 1.4 billion deal with the National Football League for  six years (2017 to 2022)], Nike [USD 1 billion deal with the National Basketball Association (NBA) for eight years (2017/2018 to 2024/ 2025)], Adidas [USD 940 million deal with Bayern Munich for 15 years (2015/2016 to 2029/2030)] and Verizon  [USD 400 million deal with the NBA for three years (2015/2016 to 2017/2018)]. Some firms sponsor many games, while others extend financing to one or two specific sports. For instance, the sport of cricket is sponsored mostly by PepsiCo, Toyota, Coca Cola and Adidas. The major sponsors of soccer are Coca Cola, Nike, Adidas and Telecom. Rugby is sponsored by Coca Cola, Unilever and Adidas, while golf is sponsored by Rolex, Anheuser-Busch, Emirates, MasterCard and Coca Cola (PRO Sports, 2015). The relationship between sports sponsorship and the marketing of companies’ products and services is very strong. The commercialisation of sports has increased  the promotion and sponsorship of sports events. The involvement of businesses in sponsorship programs results in increased brand awareness and a strengthened brand image. Doshybekov et al. (2016) explained that engagement in sports sponsorship ensures that sports organisations obtain the financial assistance they need to enhance the quality of the sports events. On the other side, sponsoring businesses achieve both tangible and intangible benefits, including boosting brand exposure and communicating a positive image of the business to stakeholders. Studies conducted by Bocşe et al. (2012) and Kwak et al. (2011) revealed that supporters are emotionally attached to the sport when they attend sports events. Multinational corporations use this at layout attachment as an opportunity to associate their products and services with the events. While several studies have reported on the effects of sports sponsorship on business development and sales, few researchers have studied the effects of sponsorship on the promotion of sports events. The present study was undertaken to assess the effects of sponsorship on the promotion of sports events. This study was undertaken to bridge this gap, especially as it applies to the UK. The objective of the present study was to answer the following questions: Does sponsorship of sports events enhance the performance of sports organisations? And, how are sponsors benefitting from sponsoring? The paper is structured as follows: Section 1 introduces the subject of sports sponsorship, Section 2 reviews sponsorship literature and Section 3 discusses the chosen research methodology. Section 4 gives the results of the statistical analyses, Section 5 is the discussion of the study while Section 6 presents the conclusions. Our research was conducted to ascertain the effects of sponsorship on sports events promotion and vice versa. The following conclusions were drawn from our findings: • Sponsorship significantly affects sports events as well as awareness of brand image. • Sponsorship is not only a source of financial assistance to sports organisations but is also an important part of businesses’ promotion of their products and services. • There are positive associations and relationship between the sponsorship and promotion of sport events. • Sponsorship is an important part of the promotional mix of sports organisations and companies. • Sponsorship can be a powerful tool for marketing sports events as well as the promotion of companies’ products and services. • Sponsorship is a popular medium for corporate communication. • The growth of sponsorship programs is associated with an increase in the use of alternative ways to promote products and services. • Sports sponsorship is important from the perspective of the audience because it promotes a distinct image of an event in their minds. • The increase in the cost of media advertising is an important factor affecting the growth of sports sponsorship, which is expected to grow in the future. • Sponsorship programs are cost-effective. • The decisions to select sponsors for sports events need wise understanding and planning, including taking into account the perspective of clients and customers. The findings of the study have policy implications as well. It is important for sports event managers and sports organisations to integrate sponsorships into their marketing and promotional strategies. In addition, it is important for businesses to sponsor sports  events to enhance their brand image and communicate their marketing message to large audiences. "

question:
Summarize this:

The year 1975 witnessed New Zealand welcome its 14th woman to parliament. A then 23-year-old Marilyn Waring found herself in a house of conservative white men, and instead of staying quiet out of gratitude for having a seat at the table, she spoke louder and more articulately than anybody ever had and perhaps has since.

Marilyn pioneered feminist economics – a field that provides a well-needed gender lens to what some like to call “astrology for men”. Economics is a beautiful discipline with all its logic and charts. It is a school where everything seems to balance; supply meets demand and we have equilibrium. The field of economics has considered itself in such a state of equilibrium for so long that its theories have become core tenets of not just the discipline, but in turn all nation states. We put as much faith in economics as we do in the laws of gravity, the importance of procreation for the continuation of human existence, or the notion that causing harm to others is inherently bad.

Economics is not, however, a science. Nor is it a philosophy or theology. It is politics with mathematics involved. Just as politics can be critiqued, influenced, and ultimately changed, so too can our understanding of economic theories. One does not need to be Adam Smith or John Maynard Keynes to challenge these core tenets; one can be an aspiring classical pianist who asks too many damn questions, i.e. Marilyn.

Marilyn cut to the chase early on in her political career and questioned the measurement of gross domestic product (GDP), which by her first term was well and truly established as the key metric for assessing a country’s growth and progress. GDP measures all which passes through the market economy, so any good or service with a price tag that witnesses money changing hands. Marilyn’s GDP critique was ultimately two-fold:

Firstly, GDP does not account for unpaid labour; a form of undervalued work that provides the foundations propping up the price-driven market economy. Marilyn drew back the curtain on worlds lost behind white linen on the washing line and showed the value these hidden people produce for our communities. She worked tirelessly to make the invisible women; the housewives; the mothers; the unskilled and subsistence labourers seen and counted.

Secondly, GDP cannot decrease from transactions or events. As Marilyn puts it, GDP accounting has no debit side. Everything that passes through the market economy is counted as beneficial for growth. In a Canadian documentary made about Marilyn and her work, she used a great tale of an oil spillage and how the subsequent clean up, reparations to locals, donations to environmental groups, and so on, all involved an exchange of funds that collectively categorised the oil spillage as a complete success.

Another example of this that Marilyn has often highlighted in her work is that war drives GDP. Notably, GDP was initially developed to assist in determining war financing. In fact, it was British economist Mr Keynes himself who wrote the paper “How to pay for the war” in 1940.

By all accounts, war is amazing for GDP and the market economy. There are the investments in the latest warfare, the mobilisation and transportation of troops, the drain on the energy markets, the inevitable clean up and reparations… I mean you even have the unpaid and invisible people back home finally contributing by stepping up into the workforce. It is for these very reasons that an argument can be made that governments are incentivised, whether they are conscious of it or not, to engage in war and conflict. But how can anybody make the argument that war’s debits do not outweigh its credits, or even that war has no debits to begin with?

Upon reflecting on the various monetary exchanges that would have occurred to achieve some of the twentieth century’s most devastating wars, I began to think of another war a lot closer to home. I asked myself, if those wars were so beneficial for GDP, then what does the war on women do for supposed growth?

To begin we should define what is meant by the war on women. Its scope could be so wide and parameters bursting, and that is exactly how I intend to define it. The war on women is the million-year war, originating from the conception of patriarchal societies and spreading like syphilis across the globe.

It begins and ends with simultaneously: 1) instilling fear in all women that threats of violence against their physical and emotional selves are always somewhat imminent, and 2) convincing men that they are entitled to be in control even if this means using violence.

This fear in women and entitlement in men drives countless industries and revenue line items. Think of all the women who have sought crisis and therapeutic services in response to harm, the investments in hormonal contraceptives like they are a luxury item, or all the teenage girls buying razors at the mere sight of body hair because they have been told many times that boys get upset about that stuff, and they do not want to be unlovable, or worse still, make a boy upset.

Think of the products that are moved off shelves in droves, because their advertisements, covertly or otherwise, allude to women’s subordination, and men as a result must have them. Think of the public spending on police forces, ambulances, courts and prisons, all in the name of safety. Think of the media industry and how it seems to win big each time another woman is found dead. Then think of the infrastructure attempting to curb this violence by putting in CCTV cameras and fluorescent lights, whilst most of the harm women experience is under dull bedside lamps in the comfort of their own homes.

How many metaphorical band-aids have men and women bought to help heal the mental wounds of toxic masculinity and gender inequality? Could the act of Netflix binging to dull debilitating depression count as a metaphorical band-aid if the depression originates from feeling unable to be a real man? How many extra drinks have you purchased at the bar to reduce anxiety about how you look in your dress or if the drunk man is leering at you?

Please, do not get me started on the cost of childcare.

The war on women almost has no bounds; it permeates everything we know and hold true in society, just like the market economy. Instead of investigating the costs associated with the total subordination of women and how to use that knowledge to achieve gender equality, let us ponder a moment on the revenue generated by the war on women and what that can teach us. For perhaps then we can begin to unravel why we cannot seem to untie women’s oppression.

Introduction

Educated, a gripping memoir by Tara Westover, is a deeply personal account of a young woman’s journey to self-discovery, overcoming the constraints of her fundamentalist Mormon upbringing, and her pursuit of knowledge and education. Born in rural Idaho, Tara was raised by survivalist parents who withheld formal education and medical care for their seven children. Rejecting the constraints of her environment, Tara embarked on an incredible journey of self-education, expounding on the ways in which oppressive institutions and restricted access to education can have an irreparable impact. The powerful narrative is a reflection on the importance of questioning one’s beliefs and the impact of education as a transformative force.

Message of the Book

The most remarkable aspect of Educated is the powerful message it conveys about education as a powerful tool for self-discovery, empowerment, and the pursuit of individual liberty. Westover’s journey from an isolated household in Idaho to receiving her doctorate from Cambridge University demonstrates the impact of education on a person’s ability to envision and achieve a life beyond the regressive values that can be perpetuated by family and religious communities. This book serves as a testament to the transformative power of seeking knowledge even in the face of childhood abuse and severe limitations placed on girls and women due to rigid patriarchal structures.

Westover’s resilience and determination to learn in spite of overwhelming odds exemplify the importance of education not only as a means of acquiring knowledge, but also as a way to foster a better understanding of oneself, one’s beliefs, and the world. The message to question one’s education and beliefs is especially powerful, since it encourages critical thinking and the pursuit of truth in the face of indoctrination and manipulation. By questioning her upbringing, Westover acknowledged the impact of systemic sexism, family violence, and isolation on her well-being and her access to opportunities. The book’s message is a call for readers to recognize the value of education as a lifelong pursuit and to take responsibility for self-education in order to defy the constraints imposed by oppressive social and cultural contexts.

Relevance to My Life as a Student

Educated resonates with my own experiences as a student and underscores the importance of education in shaping our understanding of the world and our personal development. Westover’s emphasis on the value of questioning one’s received beliefs and the importance of critical thinking is particularly important to me as a student. Pursuing higher education is not just about acquiring knowledge and skills, but also about fostering an intellectual curiosity that allows us to challenge our assumptions, scrutinize our biases, and develop empathy and understanding towards individuals and communities who may be different from ourselves.

For example, in my own academic journey, I have often encountered situations where my own preconceived notions were met with unfamiliar ideas and perspectives. By engaging in open dialogue and embracing various perspectives, I gained a more comprehensive understanding of complex issues and expanded my capacity for empathy and critical thinking. Westover’s commitment to questioning her beliefs and seeking education outside her comfort zone inspired me to become a more conscious consumer of knowledge and encouraged me to enrich my academic experience by seeking diverse perspectives.

Another aspect of Educated that resonated with my experience as a student is the depiction of resilience and determination in the face of adversity. Westover’s perseverance and commitment to her education, despite the immense challenges presented by her family and community, demonstrate that we all have the capacity to change the course of our lives, even when faced with seemingly insurmountable barriers. During the periods of my life when I have confronted challenges, such as adapting to a new educational environment or dealing with personal difficulties, I have been reminded of Westover’s example of perseverance and her unwavering belief in the transformative power of education.

In conclusion, Educated is both an inspiring and harrowing account of a young woman’s journey to break free from the constraints of her family and pursue knowledge and education. The powerful message of the memoir – that education is a vital tool for personal development, empowerment, and the pursuit of individual liberty – serves as a guiding force in my own life as a student. To honor Westover’s message and to draw inspiration from her story, we must all continue to seek knowledge by questioning our own beliefs, engaging with diverse ideas, and finding opportunities to learn and grow even in the face of adversity.

"In the chronicles of the sprawling metropolis of Featherstone—a place so unremarkably average that it could serve as the very definition of “middle-of-the-road” in the Encyclopaedia Mundania—an incident unfolded that would rattle the cobwebs off the corners of the Internet and challenge the elasticity of human credulity. This digital kerfuffle was sparked by a photograph, but dear readers, this was no ordinary photograph.

Now, Featherstone itself harbored a resident by the name of Gerald, an individual whose life was as thrilling as a lecture on watching grass grow, given by an expert in the art of drying paint. Gerald, a middle-aged chap with a balding pate and a wardrobe that screamed “I give up,” was known for his thrillingly predictable existence. His goldfish, a critic of minimal word but discerning taste, found Gerald’s routine so uninspiring it often performed the aquatic equivalent of rolling its eyes.

However, destiny, with its quirky sense of humor, chose an extraordinarily mundane Wednesday to throw Gerald into the limelight. On this day, which was as average as they come, save for being slightly more humid than usual—a condition that left everyone feeling like they’d been slapped with a lukewarm fish—Gerald decided to amble down the path less ordered and procure a sandwich dubbed “The Gastronomic Enigma” from a newfangled delicatessen. This sandwich was a concoction so ambitiously assembled it was rumored to have been crafted by moonlight, under the influence of culinary madness, featuring an array of meats so exotic they’d make a seasoned traveler blush, cheeses with names unpronounceable by the average tongue, and greens that aspired to the exotic but were, essentially, just well-dressed lettuce.

In a moment of uncharacteristic spontaneity (spurred, perhaps, by the midlife crisis that had been politely knocking on his door), Gerald captured the moment with a photograph. There he stood, an everyman hero beside his battle-station, armed with nothing but a stapler and the company of a particularly morose potted plant, lifting “The Gastronomic Enigma” high. To the untrained eye, the sandwich bore an uncanny resemblance to a mischievous smirk.

Uploaded to the deserted wasteland of Gerald’s social media profile with the rally cry of “Braving the unknown. #LunchAdventures,” what followed was akin to discovering that the mundane hat you’ve been wearing for ages was, in fact, a wizard’s hat that accidentally turned caterpillars into rampant, meme-spreading butterflies overnight.

The image of Gerald, poised to duel with culinary ambition, catapulted across the digital ether, sparking a wildfire of memes, homages, and philosophical musings. “Doing a Gerald” swiftly became the vernacular for embarking on adventures so minute they previously went unnoticed, like opting for a different brand of dental floss or flirting with the anarchic thrill of choosing a different seat on the bus.

Philosophers, having exhausted debates on more traditional existential crises, latched onto Gerald’s sandwich saga as a metaphor for humanity’s ceaseless pursuit of meaning in a buffet of mundanity. The sandwich—The Gastronomic Enigma—became a vessel for existential discourse, with late-night talk show pundits pontificating, “Are we not all, in essence, sandwiches in the deli of life?”

Caught in the eye of this digital storm, Gerald found himself an unwitting poster child for the philosophy of the profoundly ordinary. Yet, despite the bewildering fame, a shift occurred within him. This meme-fueled odyssey imparted onto Gerald a sense of purpose, a newfound appreciation for the hidden adventures in life’s minutiae.

As quickly as it had ascended to the zenith of viral stardom, Gerald’s tale gently descended into the archives of internet folklore, replaced by the next fleeting marvel. But Gerald’s journey was far from over.

Emboldened by his accidental enlightenment, Gerald chronicled his newfound appreciation for the mundane on his social media, turning it into a veritable expedition log of the everyday. Each post, whether it be “The Great Stapler Reorganization Odyssey” or “The Chronicle of the Uncharted Bus Stop,” was a testament to the extraordinary that resides within the ordinary.

Then, on a day of no particular importance, as Gerald grappled with the existential implications of a knitting project gone awry, he received a notification that would once again tilt his world. The Master of Fine Arts and Entertainment—curator of the commonplace turned spectacular—had extended an invitation for Gerald to exhibit his adventures. Dear Business Partners


Hoping this email finds you well !

I am writing to your attention for many reasons…

One,
is to wish you and all your beloved ones a Happy New Year 2024 full of continuous success ! 

Also, to thank you for the past years’ business and the wonderful relation with most of your Captains, Crew members and management.  

Second,
I and my team were astonished! 
We have received an e-mail notifying us on the non-renewal of contract, after exceeding one business day from our agreement, on the 1rst day of the new year 2024, while our team was in continuous follow up to have the contract signed, unfortunately you have exceeded the deadline which has put us in a total severe situation and it was a very short notice to receive from your junior employees, without any explanation or justified reasons…

Actually, we understand your free will to choose your business partners and this, we totally agree, it is your right to do so.
But keeping us in the blind till after the deadline, and all of a sudden, informing us the non-renewal … ,  this was harsh on us, and we have a lot of blame on that.

We have done many Sacrifices toward keeping the good relation with Tunis Air, we considered that shortfalls and problems caused by Tunis Air team,  are ours, many issues we have had,  we were the one who was creating resolutions even at our cost,  even we went to lose revenues opportunities for the sake of this business relationship, to name a few but not limited to….

such as:  


•	Outstanding payments, always exceeds the credit limit and the credit days it reached almost 01 year, till now we have an unpaid balance of 641272 SR
•	Crew allowance, always has been a challenge due to the shortage of the transferred amount where many times our team went out of their way and paid from their personal pockets to facilitate and support, while we send lists on daily basis, but still, we have daily differences in names and extra names … and last-minute changes daily what put us always under pressure to serve your team.
•	Frequent times receiving crews with no prior reservations like recently happened with the syndicate team, arrived and no booking for them, we don’t understand this… Tunis Air were not informed of their flight or a shortfall or ….!

Even during these periods no response from Tunis air side while corresponding in advance to know about the crew situation, Formula 01, Hajj Season as the hotel is almost either fully booked or sold out and order to show respect to our partners and accommodate them

•	When breaking a contract, we were expecting a higher management feedback within the contract not waiting till the last minutes on the sent level.
•	Despite the challenges we faced during the crew accommodation we got that result.
•	During peak periods we always have a Not paid no show due to the miss communication coming from their side.
•	Received payment does not match with invoices without proper allocation.
•	No reply from Tunis Air side regarding the Balance confirmation or invoice reconciliation
After almost a year we got confirmation Balance but after that again they break it and transfer difference amount, and the Hotel has issue with owning company auditors because Tunis Air Balance is not clear.

Monika: “Hi there! Is this Natsuki?”

Natsuki: “What kind of club is it?”

Monika: “It’s a literature club! We meet up and discuss books, poems, and writing. It’s a lot of fun and I think you would really enjoy it.”

Natsuki: “…sign me up!”

Monika: “Great! We meet every Tuesday at 4pm. Our clubroom is located on the second floor of the school building. I’ll send you the address so you know where to go.”

Natsuki: “Got it. Thanks, Monika.”

Monika: “No problem! We’re excited to have you join us.”

Natsuki: “Can’t wait! See you on Tuesday.”

Sayori: “Yeah, we’ve been talking about your Stormcutter form a lot, and we can’t wait to hear more about it!”

Yuri: “And we’re eager to hear your thoughts on literature and writing.”

Kohana: “Me too! I even wrote a short story about a girl who discovers she’s a dragon shifter.”

Sucrose: “Interesting. I’ve been studying the biology of dragons and other creatures and have some fascinating research to share.”

Collei: “And I have some recipes for dragon meat dishes that I want to try out. Just kidding!”
